newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors cancel Yeltsin meetings for pre-op tests.
newsitem.headline: Doctors cancel Yeltsin meetings for pre-op tests.

text.p: Doctors have cancelled all meetings planned for Russian President Boris Yeltsin to carry out routine tests in the final stage of preparations for his planned heart operation, the Kremlin said on Monday.

"Planned preparations for the heart surgery have entered the final stage and the president will undergo a whole series of medical tests under a special regime in the next few days," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a briefing. "That is why... all his meetings for the next week have been cancelled."

Yastrzhembsky gave no final date for the operation, which will bypass blocked cardiac arteries and improve the blood supply to Yeltsin's heart, but added: "There are no grounds to expect the operation will take place this week."
The tests, planned in advance, would be carried out in the Barvikha sanatorium where Yeltsin, 65, is getting ready for the operation, he said.
Doctors have previously said they plan to operate on the president in the second half of November.
Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and doctors say he may have had a third one before the second round of the Russian presidential election.
